lines.meaning: to fill grand monuments with worm-holes,

lines.text: To feed oblivion with decay of things,
lines.meaning: to feed oblivion, total forgetting, with the remains of decaying things,

lines.text: To blot old books and alter their contents,
lines.meaning: to smudge (blot) old books until their contents change,

lines.text: To pluck the quills from ancient ravens' wings,
lines.meaning: to pull the feathers (quills) from the wings of ancient ravens,
lines.why: Ravens were said to live very long, so even the oldest of them loses its feathers to Time.

lines.text: To dry the old oak's sap and cherish springs,
lines.meaning: to dry up the old oak's sap while nourishing young shoots (springs),

lines.text: To spoil antiquities of hammer'd steel,
lines.meaning: to ruin ancient things made of hammered steel,

lines.text: And turn the giddy round of Fortune's wheel;
lines.meaning: and to keep turning the dizzy (giddy) wheel of Fortune.
lines.why: Fortune was pictured as a goddess turning a great wheel, lifting some people up and dropping others down. Time keeps it turning, so luck keeps changing.

summary: Lucrece lists the ways Time wears down and changes everything.
